thread:
Samir: Heads-up — while validating the seqlen=512 workload on H100 with torch.compile + CUDA graphs I saw a ~40% token/sec regression vs master yesterday. Anyone else seeing this?

Maria Chen: uhh that's bad. quick numbers?

Samir: baseline (no compile/cudagraph): ~18k tokens/s
with torch.compile+cudagraph: ~11k tokens/s
same model, same batch distribution. Regression first showed up after the autotuner change that landed yesterday (arch-aware picks).

Devon R.: do you have profiler traces? nvtx / Nsight?

Samir: yes, attached snippet from perf run (trimmed):

```
[Profiler] seq=512 batch=4 H100
cudaKernel: fused_attn_v2    42.1%  (master)
cudaKernel: generic_gemm     61.8%  (after-autotune)
cublasLtGemm:  18.4% total
kernel_launch_overhead increased ~2.3x
```

Samir: autotuner picked generic_gemm path for this seqlen on H100. fused_attn_v2 was faster in non-cudagraph runs, but cudagraph capture seems to be forcing a different code path and we lose fused kernels in the capture.

bench-bot: bench-1234 completed: seed=2026 model=redwood-small seqlen=512 batch=4 gpu=H100
metrics: tokens_per_s=11045 latency_p50=23.1ms

Josh: interesting — could be that torch.compile+capture inlines shapes differently and the kernel-hash for cuda-graph doesn't match fused_attn_v2 variant so runtime falls back. We had a similar-looking fallback in the old dynshape pilot.

Maria Chen: confirm: does disabling cudagraph restore fused_attn picks?

Samir: quick test: disable cudagraph -> tokens_per_s=17680. So yes, disabling restores perf.

Devon R.: sounds like kernel selection key includes runtime capture flags. Autotuner may have stored key with capture=false so capture=true mismatches. Can you repro with small repro and print kernel-selection key? (we log kernel keys at debug: RW_KERNEL_KEY)

Samir: posted debug logs:

```
RW_KERNEL_KEY: model=redwood-small seqlen=512 batch=4 arch=H100 capture=false quant=fp16 kernel=fused_attn_v2
RW_KERNEL_KEY: model=redwood-small seqlen=512 batch=4 arch=H100 capture=true  quant=fp16 kernel=generic_gemm
```

Samir: so the autotuner DB has capture=false entry. When capture=true we should still prefer fused_attn if available. Seems the runtime ranking isn't architecture-aware across the capture dimension.

Josh: two-prong fix:
- acknowledge kernel key should treat capture flag as soft-preference, not hard mismatch (i.e., allow compatible kernels across capture/private flags)
- add autotuner sweep for capture=true on H100 for seqlen buckets we care about

Maria Chen: agree. short-term mitigation: add env RW_RUNTIME_FORCE_KERNEL=fused_attn_v2 to the canary flutter and roll to affected Dedicated pools.

Devon R.: I'll open ENG-4123 with profiling attachments and assign. We should also add an integration test that runs torch.compile+cudagraph matrix to catch this.

Samir: thanks. I pushed a small change to runtime to log when a kernel fallback across capture happens (PR #3981). Also adding a canary job to perf CI.

bench-bot: created task perf-ci/torchcompile-cudagraph H100 run queued

Maria Chen: great. follow-ups: (1) DEVON: ENG-4123, (2) BENCH/BOT: schedule 24h sweep, (3) PLATFORM: apply RW_RUNTIME_FORCE_KERNEL in canary.

Josh: FYI: potential risk — forcing fused_attn in capture may break capture compatibility if kernel uses dynamic allocations. need to validate correctness QA before large roll.

Devon R.: noted. I'll include validation harness (compare logits + kv-cache sync tests) in ENG-4123.

Samir: thanks all. I'll collect full nvprof trace and drop into the ticket.

Maria Chen: :thumbsup:
